Write-ups of short projects done in the lab, mostly undergraduate research
(IPRE) and rotations. A two-month project rarely ends in a paper, but it does
end with a question that was asked, an analysis that was run, and a list of
things that went wrong or are still open. Those are worth keeping, so the next
student starts from where the last one stopped.

## Projects

::: {#project-pages}
:::

## How to read these pages

The results here are exploratory. They come from short projects, have not been
peer reviewed, and each page lists the reasons to be careful with them. Use
them as a starting point for your own analysis, and check with Tomás before
citing or building on a specific result.

## Adding a project

One page per project, written when the project ends. Keep it to what a new
student needs:

- **The question**, and why this cell type, region, or cohort.
- **Data and methods**, with enough detail to rerun it: which files, which
  packages, which thresholds, which model.
- **What came out**, including results that were null or hard to interpret.
- **Caveats**: what would have to be checked before trusting the result.
- **Next steps**: what you would do with another month.

Ask the student before publishing a page with their name on it. Don't include
their IPRE report form or anything else with personal identifiers, and don't
include results from controlled-access data (see
[Databases](../databases/index.qmd)).
